answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network anchors agent identities to a cryptographic stake-burning jetty. Registering each additional agent requires burning tokens at a superlinear cost scaling as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$, creating insurmountable economic friction for clone swarms. Like carving verification proofs into marble, burnt stakes are permanently slashed, while identity commitments gleam through zero-knowledge opal rings.
